title: Siemens Healthineers Launches Olyrian Diagnostics Carve-Out
text: Siemens Healthineers Launches Olyrian Diagnostics Carve-Out Siemens Healthineers initiates the separation of its in vitro diagnostics unit into Olyrian Diagnostics, rebranding to Healthineers in a move finalized by mid-2028. Siemens Healthineers officially announced on November 5, 2026, that it has initiated the formal carve-out process for its in vitro diagnostics business. This strategic move establishes the foundational step toward creating a fully independent entity that will operate under the new name Olyrian Diagnostics. The announcement signals a significant structural shift for the global medical technology giant, aiming to unlock distinct value for both the new standalone diagnostics company and the parent organization. Parallel Corporate Restructuring StrategySimultaneously with the diagnostic unit separation, Siemens Healthineers confirmed it will rebrand itself as Healthineers. The two transitions are scheduled to take place in parallel, ensuring operational continuity during the complex restructuring phase. Olyrian Diagnostics adopts the purpose statement Powering human potential at the heart of care to define its future trajectory. This branding change reflects an unwavering commitment to placing people at the center of healthcare innovations and workflows.Olyrian Operational Timeline And ScopeThe transition to a standalone organizational structure for Olyrian is expected to be completed by mid-2028. Establishing this dedicated name and brand gives the business a distinct market presence as one of the largest stand-alone diagnostics-focused companies globally. From patient draw to population health, Olyrian will deliver diagnostic solutions for both laboratory and point-of-care testing environments. The company emphasizes that informed and connected workflows drive efficiency and empower a more comprehensive understanding of patient health.Stakeholder Roles And Customer ImpactSharon Bracken, Head of Diagnostics at Siemens Healthineers, stated that Olyrian defines the next chapter by combining intelligent technology with the expertise of care teams. While working toward independence, Olyrian Diagnostics remains part of Siemens Healthineers, and customers can expect the same commitment to quality, service, and innovation. As of November 5, 2026, there is no change to products, services, contracts, service levels, or customer points of contact. Any future changes will be communicated directly to stakeholders as the carve-out evolves.Historical Diagnostic Innovation LegacyThe Olyrian business traces its roots to Siemens Healthineers acquisitions in 2006 and 2007 of three companies with histories dating back to 1884. Today, the entity manufactures more than 16 billion tests annually across an assay portfolio addressing nearly every major disease area. Its history includes pioneering the first urine test strip for diabetes and the first automated, integrated clinical chemistry and immunoassay analyzer. The current portfolio encompasses laboratory automation, informatics, and point-of-care testing solutions to support critical diagnostic answers.Future Market Positioning StrategyOlyrian positions itself to advance diagnostics from the laboratory to the point of care, ensuring patients receive timely and accurate medical information. The new structure allows the diagnostics unit to focus singularly on in vitro diagnostics without the broader constraints of a conglomerate. This separation is designed to accelerate innovation and responsiveness in a rapidly evolving healthcare market. The company remains proud of its century-long legacy while preparing for a future defined by specialized diagnostic excellence.
